caption: What if Africa split in two? It's already happening, very slowly. The East African Rift runs for thousands of kilometres from Ethiopia to Mozambique, where the Nubian and Somali plates pull apart about 6-7 mm a year. That's roughly 6 times slower than your fingernails grow. But the rift can jump: in 2005, magma tore open a 60 km stretch in Ethiopia's Afar region, up to 8 m wide, in about three weeks. That viral 2018 crack in Kenya? Geologists say heavy rain mostly washed soft volcanic ash out of older ground. The rift even built Ol Doinyo Lengai in Tanzania, whose lava comes out black at about 500 °C and turns white within days. In millions of years, the sea could flood in and form a new ocean. Plot twist: India did this first, breaking away near Madagascar and racing north at up to ~20 cm a year. Which side would YOU pick? 👇
